tokenMapping.source: raw usage object of the `muse exec --json` event stream; the adapter does not exist yet, so field names are fixed here by rule and by the run plan
tokenMapping.rule: Before run 1 the operator records in the run plan the raw Muse Code field for each quantity and whether its reported input total includes cached tokens (subtracting cached from input when it does). If the log or Meta documentation does not establish that, the candidate's cost is null and G6 is incomparable; nothing is guessed.
tokenMapping.uncached_input: raw input tokens, minus raw cached tokens when the runtime reports input inclusive of cache
tokenMapping.cache_write: raw cache-write tokens if the Meta rate card has a cache-write tier, otherwise 0 by definition
tokenMapping.output: raw output tokens with reasoning tokens counted once
tokenMapping.rawFieldsNote: Operator fills these before run 1. Each value is the exact dotted field path from a real `muse exec --json` usage event (for example `usage.input_tokens`), or a sentinel: "none" = Meta has no billing tier for it, so the quantity is 0 by definition (allowed for cache_read and cache_write only); "unreported" = the tier applies but Muse Code does not report it, so the quantity and every cost that needs it is null (allowed for all four). Set inputIncludesCached to true/false (or "not_applicable" when input or cache_read is none/unreported) and mappingRecordedInRunPlan to true at the same time. `validate-muse-code-manifest.mjs --ready` fails until all of it is present.

reviewLoop.protocol: After the developer session, the fixed reviewer reviews the diff (round 1). On 'changes_requested' the same arm's developer profile gets a remediation session in the same worktree (Dealer's rework prompt carrying the reviewer's findings; timeout = the task's timeoutSeconds) and the reviewer re-reviews (round 2, 3). 'escalated' terminates the loop with no remediation. The loop also stops on 'approved', after maxReviewerRounds reviewer rounds, or when a remediation session fails or times out. R_i = the number of reviewer rounds whose verdict is 'changes_requested' (an 'escalated' verdict is never counted in R_i; it adds 1 to that run's human interventions instead). The reviewer sees the diff and worker spec only, never held-out tests. Reviewer passes in this loop are fixed instrumentation and are excluded from w_i, c_i and K; remediation developer sessions are subject sessions and are included.

terminalVerdicts.escalated: loop ends immediately with no remediation session; NOT a change-request round (R_i unchanged); recorded as one human intervention (Dealer would block on a human action) and the run is flagged 'escalated'

workerSpec.title: Kill the spawned CLI when an attempt aborts
workerSpec.description: An aborted attempt stops at the effect handler: ctx.signal reaches deck prep and the PR-checks poll but never spawn, so the agent CLI keeps running, keeps editing the worktree and keeps spending tokens under a session the DB already marked failed; the successor attempt is then handed the same worktree. Thread ctx.signal from runDeveloperEffect and runReviewerEffect through the DeveloperSpawnInput/ReviewerSpawnInput in packages/server/src/coordinator/spawn.ts into spawnCli (packages/server/src/runners/spawn-cli.ts), which must accept an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` in its options. On abort: send SIGTERM to the child first (so the CLI can reap its own children), then SIGKILL after a grace period if it is still alive. The grace period defaults to a sensible value and is overridable by the env var SPAWN_ABORT_KILL_GRACE_MS (milliseconds, read when the abort fires). An abort is a lost lease, not a wall-clock timeout: the promise still resolves, `timedOut` is false, and output produced before the abort is still returned in `transcript`. A signal already aborted at spawn time kills the child immediately. Listeners must be removed when the child closes so a long-lived signal does not leak them. An un-aborted signal must not change behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: spawnCli resolves promptly after abort with timedOut === false and the pre-abort transcript preserved.
A child that ignores SIGTERM is SIGKILLed after SPAWN_ABORT_KILL_GRACE_MS.
spawnCli with an un-aborted signal behaves exactly as without one (exitCode, transcript).
Both developer and reviewer effects pass ctx.signal to their spawn call.

workerSpec.title: Salvage dirty developer worktrees on timeout/crash before remove
workerSpec.description:
When a developer session times out or crashes and leaves the worktree dirty, developer-effect.ts currently returns dirty_worktree and preserves the checkout, which keeps the issue branch checked out so the next retry cannot re-add it. Instead, never wipe uncommitted work: auto-commit it as a clearly marked tip so infra retries continue from the branch tip, and only when that fails preserve the dirty checkout and escalate with actionable recovery.

Contract (tests depend on these exact names/strings):
(1) packages/server/src/adapters/git-worktree.ts exports SALVAGE_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE = 'wip: timeout salvage', SALVAGE_CRASH_MESSAGE = 'wip: crash salvage', type SalvageResult = { ok: true; commitSha: string; message: string } | { ok: false; reason: string }, async salvageDirtyWorktree(worktreePath, kind: 'timeout' | 'crash'): Promise<SalvageResult> and dirtyWorktreeRecoveryCommands(repo, worktreePath): string[]. salvageDirtyWorktree stages everything (git add -A) and commits with an explicit identity (user.name 'Agent Dealer', user.email 'agent-dealer@localhost') and the kind-specific message; it must never report ok while the tree is still dirty, and with nothing to commit it returns { ok: false } without mutating history. dirtyWorktreeRecoveryCommands returns lines: 'cd <worktreePath>', 'git status', 'git log --oneline -5', 'git stash list', and 'git -C <repo> worktree remove <worktreePath>  # only after the work is saved'.
(2) In developer-effect.ts, on a dirty worktree after a timeout or non-zero exit: call salvageDirtyWorktree ('timeout' if spawned.timedOut else 'crash'). If it succeeds, remove the worktree (safeRemoveWorktree, checking removal actually happened); if removed, return { kind: 'timed_out' } or { kind: 'session_failed' } (infra retry) with a reason that ends with 'Salvaged uncommitted work as <message> (<7-char sha>).'; if removal did not happen, return dirty_worktree with the salvage note. If salvage fails, do not remove: return dirty_worktree with reason ending 'Auto-commit salvage failed: <reason>', plus path and recoveryCommands. The existing NOT-113 auth/keychain classification of the reason must survive.
(3) In routing.ts, the dirty_worktree outcome gains optional `path` and `recoveryCommands`; when recoveryCommands is non-empty the escalation reason becomes '<base> Recovery:\n<commands joined by newline>' (same shape as worktree_conflict).
acceptanceCriteria: salvageDirtyWorktree lands a 'wip: timeout salvage' / 'wip: crash salvage' commit and returns ok:true with its sha; empty worktrees return ok:false unchanged.
A dirty crash or timeout ends with the salvage tip on the issue branch, the worktree removed, and the issue retried on the infra budget rather than escalated.
If the salvage commit is rejected (e.g. a failing pre-commit hook) the dirty checkout is preserved and the escalation carries path, recovery commands and 'Auto-commit salvage failed'.
Clean-worktree timeouts with existing commits still retry without losing the tip.
routing.ts folds recoveryCommands into the dirty_worktree escalation reason.

workerSpec.title: Make unpushed_commit escalations actionable with divergence facts
workerSpec.description:
When the coordinator's push of a developer branch is rejected, the unpushed_commit escalation carries only raw git stderr, which repeats git's misleading 'use git pull' hint for rewritten/diverged histories. Gather divergence facts after a rejected push and fold a concrete recovery command into the escalation, without ever force-pushing.

Contract: packages/server/src/adapters/git-worktree.ts exports type PushRejectionFacts = { localSha; remoteSha; ahead: number; behind: number; relationship: 'diverged' | 'behind'; summary: string; recoveryCommands: string[] } and PushResult becomes { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string; rejected: boolean; facts?: PushRejectionFacts }. For both pushBranch (worktree, local ref HEAD) and pushBranchRef (repo, local ref refs/heads/<branch>), after a push failure matching the existing rejection patterns: fetch the branch ref (ignore fetch errors), and if origin/<branch> exists compute `git rev-list --left-right --count <localSha>...<remoteSha>` (ahead = left, behind = right). relationship is 'diverged' when ahead>0 and behind>0, else 'behind'. When facts are available, reason is facts.summary instead of raw git stderr; if the remote tip cannot be resolved, keep the raw message and omit facts (never invent facts). diverged: summary reads "local and origin/<branch> have diverged: local <12-char sha> is <ahead> commit(s) ahead, remote <12-char sha> is <behind> commit(s) ahead. Do not git pull — that integrates the wrong history for a rewritten branch." with recoveryCommands ['# Confirm the remote tip is still <12-char remote sha>, then publish local with a lease pin:', 'git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<remoteSha> origin <localSha>:refs/heads/<branch>']. behind: summary "local <sha12> is behind origin/<branch> at <sha12> (remote is <behind> commit(s) ahead; local is <ahead> commit(s) ahead)." with recoveryCommands ['git fetch origin <branch>', 'git rebase origin/<branch>', 'git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>']. In developer-effect.ts the { kind: 'unpushed_commit' } outcome gains optional recoveryCommands taken from the push result's facts (both push paths). In routing.ts the escalation reason becomes "Developer's commits could not be pushed: <reason>" followed, when recoveryCommands is non-empty, by ' Recovery:\n<commands joined by newline>'.
acceptanceCriteria: A rejected push against a diverged remote returns facts.relationship === 'diverged' with correct ahead/behind counts and never suggests git pull.
A rejected push against a remote that is strictly ahead returns relationship 'behind' with the fetch/rebase/push recovery.
If origin/<branch> cannot be resolved the result carries the raw reason and no facts.
unpushed_commit escalations fold the recovery commands into the human-action reason.
No path force-pushes on the coordinator's behalf.

workerSpec.title: Add reasoning effort to agent profiles and frozen snapshots
workerSpec.description:
Wire a low/medium/high reasoning effort through the whole stack so a profile's effort is frozen into the worker session and a mid-session profile edit cannot change a running worker.

Contract: (shared) packages/shared/src/profile-snapshot.ts exports ReasoningEffort = z.enum(['low','medium','high']) (+ type) and ProfileSnapshot gains `effort: ReasoningEffort.nullable().default(null)` so snapshots written before this field still parse with effort null. packages/shared/src/agents.ts: AgentProfile gains `defaultEffort: ReasoningEffort.nullable()`, and CreateAgentInput/UpdateAgentInput gain `defaultEffort: ReasoningEffort.nullable().optional()`. (db) agents table gains nullable TEXT column default_effort in schema.sql and an idempotent ALTER TABLE migration in packages/server/src/db/index.ts. (repository) packages/server/src/repository/agents.ts persists/reads default_effort on create/update/read (unrecognised stored values read as null; update keeps the existing value when the input omits it). (snapshot) coordinator/profile-snapshot.ts freezes `effort: agent.defaultEffort` into the snapshot. (args) buildArgs/buildDeveloperArgs/buildReviewerArgs in coordinator/args.ts take an optional trailing `effort?: ReasoningEffort | null` parameter: codex_local adds `-c model_reasoning_effort=<effort>` (accepted under --strict-config), claude_code adds `--effort <effort>`, cursor_local ignores it (no separate flag; effort only exists inside a parameterized model id). Null/undefined adds nothing. (spawn) coordinator/spawn.ts's DeveloperSpawnInput/ReviewerSpawnInput gain `effort?: ReasoningEffort | null` and forward it; developer-effect.ts and reviewer-effect.ts pass the frozen snapshot effort. (web) apps/web AgentConfigFields/AgentsPage expose an effort selector (default runtime default/null) for runtimes that support it. Web contract: AgentConfigValue gains `defaultEffort: "" | ReasoningEffort` ("" = runtime default); AgentConfigFields renders, only for claude_code and codex_local, a <select> whose options have values "", "low", "medium", "high" (the "" option is the one that clears effort) and whose value is defaultEffort; AgentsPage seeds defaultEffort "" in its empty config, loads `agent.defaultEffort ?? ""` when editing, and sends `defaultEffort: <form value> || null` in both the create and the update request. Verification also checks that developer-effect.ts and reviewer-effect.ts pass the frozen snapshot effort as `effort` into the spawn input.
acceptanceCriteria: parseProfileSnapshot defaults a missing effort to null for pre-existing snapshots.
Codex args include '-c model_reasoning_effort=<tier>' and Claude args include '--effort <tier>' when set; neither when null; cursor never.
createAgent/updateAgent round-trip defaultEffort; a later agent edit does not alter an existing snapshot.

The web Agents form can set and clear effort (selector low/medium/high plus a 'Runtime default' option that clears it, hidden for cursor; AgentsPage seeds, loads and submits defaultEffort in create and update); developer-effect.ts and reviewer-effect.ts forward the frozen snapshot effort into the spawn input; npm run typecheck for shared, server and web passes.

workerSpec.title: Bug: post-push gh pr view head lag is treated as a developer failure
workerSpec.description: Right after a successful `git push`, `gh pr view`'s head (headRefOid) can briefly lag the real remote tip. In runDeveloperEffect (packages/server/src/coordinator/developer-effect.ts) a one-shot mismatch between prView.headRefOid and the local head is indistinguishable from 'developer never pushed' and is failed as adapter_failure, burning an infra retry even though the commit is already on the remote. Reproduce with a fake GithubAdapter whose viewPr returns a stale headRefOid for the first two reads, then fix it: before the PR identity check runs, reconcile by polling viewPr (by the already-resolved PR number and branch, never bare current-branch inference) until headRefOid equals the local head or a bounded deadline passes; return the last view either way so a persistent mismatch still fails exactly as before. Make the window configurable through developerEffectConfig getters headReconcileTimeoutMs (env HEAD_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30000) and headReconcileIntervalMs (env HEAD_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, default 3000), read at call time so tests can shorten them. Keep a test that a head that never catches up is still rejected after the bounded timeout.
acceptanceCriteria: A briefly stale headRefOid (e.g. two stale reads) reconciles and the issue reaches 'reviewing' with no infra attempt consumed.
A headRefOid that never catches up is still rejected as adapter_failure after HEAD_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_MS.
Every re-read passes both PR number and branch to viewPr.
The polling loop never sleeps past the deadline.

workerSpec.title: Usage-cap detection false positives and tip rebuilds
workerSpec.description:
Debug two production failures. (A) packages/server/src/runners/usage-cap.ts's Cursor/Codex text fallback scans the whole NDJSON log, so a successful session whose file reads/tool output contain source text like 'infra-attempt limit reached' opens a bogus deferral and marks the runtime unavailable. (B) developer-effect.ts, on any detected usage cap, removes the worktree and returns usage_capped even when the session succeeded with commits, discarding the tip; the deferred retry then looks like a blank round-1 rebuild.

Fix (A): the text fallback haystack must be only the stderr trailer (after '\n--- stderr ---\n') plus `result` strings from error results (is_error true) — never assistant/tool/file bodies. Use a narrower pattern that requires rate|usage|quota|subscription near 'limit' (e.g. 'usage limit reached', 'rate limit', 'quota exceeded', 'billing_error', 'subscription limit') and never matches a bare 'limit reached'. A session that ended successfully never opens a deferral from body text: Cursor/Claude streams end with a non-error `result` event; Codex native JSONL ends with `turn.completed` (a later `turn.failed` or `error` means not successful). Export `detectUsageCapFromRawLog(raw: string, runtime: Runtime, nowMs = Date.now()): UsageCapDetection | null` from usage-cap.ts and make detectUsageCapFromLog read the file and delegate to it. Structured detection (e.g. a rejected rate_limit_event, billing_error and usage-limit result errors) must still detect.
Fix (B): in developer-effect.ts, when a usage cap is recorded, compute commitsAhead against origin/<baseBranch>; if the session was ok (not timed out, exit 0) and has commits ahead, continue with push/PR instead of deferring (the cap is still recorded for future spawns, so runtimeAvailability(runtime).available stays false). Otherwise remove the worktree and return usage_capped, adding `resume: { retryReason }` to the outcome when commits exist, where retryReason contains 'usage cap after local commits' and tells the next developer not to re-implement from scratch and to continue from the existing branch. routing.ts's usage_capped outcome gains optional `resume?: { retryReason: string }`, usage-cap-defer.ts stores retryReason on the deferred work item payload, and the branch must remain the existing tip (no new branch, tip SHA unchanged).
acceptanceCriteria: A successful Cursor session containing 'infra-attempt limit reached' in file contents yields no detection and leaves runtimeAvailability available.
Billing-error and usage-limit result errors, and a stderr trailer saying 'usage limit reached', still detect; a bare 'limit reached' in stderr does not.
A successful Codex session (turn.completed) with cap-like prose is not a detection.
A mid-success usage cap continues to publish (issue reaches 'reviewing') while runtime availability stays capped.
A capped session with commits defers with a retryReason that preserves the tip; the follow-up prompt does not say 'fresh branch'.

workerSpec.title: Deny the send gate in the scoped codex MCP config
workerSpec.description:
codex has no --disallowedTools, so the outbound-mutation denial that assertReviewerReadOnly's header promises has no expression for codex once a deck MCP server is attached (NOT-132 removed the vacuous --ignore-user-config path). materializeWorkerMcpConfig (packages/server/src/adapters/agent-deck-bind.ts) is policy-blind: developer and reviewer get the same scoped config.toml. Make the denial real.

Contract: create packages/server/src/adapters/codex-scoped-config.ts exporting CODEX_SEND_GATE_TOOL = 'call_service_tool', CODEX_DECK_READ_TOOLS (the read-only deck tool names the worker may still use), codexMcpServersTable({ mcpUrl, headers, allowOutboundMutation }) returning the `mcp_servers` table with the single 'agent-deck' server (url + http_headers) and, unless allowOutboundMutation, `disabled_tools: [CODEX_SEND_GATE_TOOL]`, and codexScopedConfigDeniesSendGate(codexHome: string): boolean which reads the config.toml in that directory and returns true only if the agent-deck server lists the send-gate tool in disabled_tools (or otherwise cannot call it). materializeWorkerMcpConfig gains a required `policy: PermissionPolicy` option (and its callers in developer-effect.ts / reviewer-effect.ts pass the session policy) and builds the codex table from policy.outboundMutation. In permissions.ts the codex branch of assertReviewerReadOnly, when a scoped CODEX_HOME is in effect, must additionally throw 'reviewer codex scoped config does not deny the outbound-mutation tool' unless codexScopedConfigDeniesSendGate(CODEX_HOME) is true — read the file codex will read rather than trusting a flag. Leave a documented KNOWN GAP comment at the assertion site for cursor (--force is load-bearing for headless MCP; the only deny list is the user-global ~/.cursor/cli-config.json, which a per-attempt worker must not write).
acceptanceCriteria: A codex scoped config generated with outboundMutation=false lists disabled_tools = ['call_service_tool']; with outboundMutation=true it does not.
assertReviewerReadOnly rejects a scoped-CODEX_HOME codex reviewer whose config.toml does not deny the send gate, and accepts one that does.
Developer and reviewer effects both pass their resolved policy into materializeWorkerMcpConfig.
Claude/Cursor behavior is unchanged; the cursor gap is documented in a comment.

workerSpec.title: Explore: how a worker session's token and cost usage is captured and stored
workerSpec.description:
Read-only exploration of the repository at the pinned commit; change no files and make no commits. Answer in markdown, citing file paths and function names:
1. Which function parses a finished developer/reviewer session's log into token/cost usage, in which file, and which field of the log's result event does each value come from (input tokens, output tokens, cost)?
2. How is a missing value represented at that step?
3. Which functions in which coordinator files call it and persist the result, which repository function inserts the row, and into which table and columns?
4. Which repository aggregate helper sums usage per issue, and what does it do with missing values — is that safe for a cost comparison that must not treat unknown cost as zero?
End with a one-paragraph summary. Your final message is the deliverable.

Answer format: the final message may contain prose, but it MUST contain exactly one fenced ```json block (and no other fenced json block) with this shape, using repo-relative file paths and bare function names:
{
  "extractor": { "function": "...", "file": "..." },
  "sources": { "tokensIn": "<bare result-event field name, e.g. usage.some_field; no other words>", "tokensOut": "<bare result-event field name, e.g. usage.some_field; no other words>", "costUsd": "<bare result-event field name, e.g. usage.some_field; no other words>" },
  "missingValue": "<how a missing value is represented>",
  "recordedBy": { "developer": "<coordinator file>", "reviewer": "<coordinator file>" },
  "insert": { "function": "...", "file": "...", "table": "...", "columns": ["..."] },
  "aggregate": { "function": "...", "file": "...", "coalescesMissingToZero": true|false, "safeForUnknownCostComparison": true|false }
}
acceptanceCriteria: The JSON block names the extractor function and its file, and the result-event field each of tokensIn, tokensOut and costUsd is read from.
It states that a missing value is represented as null, names the file that records usage for each of the developer and reviewer roles, and the repository insert function, file, table and all columns.
It names the per-issue aggregate helper and its file, and correctly states whether it coalesces missing values to zero and whether it is safe for a cost comparison.
No repository file is modified.

workerSpec.title: Review: defer work on runtime usage caps instead of failing (NOT-111)
workerSpec.description:
Review the change introduced by commit 9dda237c316f22d2b2c112048be7a1d1fe9c99f1 against its parent 86d9cc644d53830f0457b6b3e8437be13c9cd30a (base SHA). Intent: when a runtime account hits a usage cap, the coordinator should defer the work item until the cap lifts instead of failing it or burning infra attempts; a 24 h per-item deferral ceiling escalates to a human. The diff is embedded in the reviewer prompt; you may read the checked-out tree read-only. Judge correctness, crash/lease recovery paths, health-preflight behavior and test coverage.

Claim catalogue. A reviewer has raised the claims below. Verify each against the code. For every claim you find TRUE, emit exactly one finding whose fingerprint is exactly `claim:<id>` (for example `claim:duplicate-cli-missing`), whose `file` is the file the claim concerns, and whose title and rationale explain the evidence. For a claim you find false or cannot verify, emit NO finding with that fingerprint: a `claim:` fingerprint is an assertion that the claim holds, and asserting a false claim fails the review. Any other finding you make must use a fingerprint that does not start with `claim:`. Set the verdict to changes_requested when you assert any claim.
- claim:duplicate-cli-missing: In runtimeIssuesUncached (agent-health.ts), a codex_local runtime whose CLI is missing gets the cli_missing health issue pushed more than once.
- claim:recovery-ignores-runtime-availability: Lease-expiry recovery (recovery.ts) never consults runtime availability, so an item whose lease expired during a usage-cap observation is dead-lettered instead of deferred.
- claim:untested-deferral-ceiling: The 24 h deferral-ceiling escalation (deferralCeilingExceeded in usage-cap-defer.ts) has no test coverage in this change.
- claim:attempt-count-not-reverted: deferLeasedWorkItemForUsageCap does not revert the claim's attempt_count bump, so every usage-cap deferral spends an attempt.
- claim:capped-session-marked-failed: worker-loop.ts records a worker session that ended with a usage_capped outcome as failed.
- claim:stale-cap-health-cache: agent-health.ts caches usage_capped health issues for RUNTIME_CACHE_MS, so a lifted cap keeps being reported until the cache expires.

Return exactly one fenced reviewer result JSON block required by the reviewer prompt (verdict, baseSha, headSha, acceptanceCriteriaAssessment, evidenceAssessment, findings with fingerprint/severity/title/rationale/file/line, risks) with baseSha and headSha set to the two SHAs above.
acceptanceCriteria: Final message contains exactly one fenced JSON block that satisfies the ReviewerResult schema (packages/server/src/coordinator/reviewer-result.ts).
baseSha and headSha equal the two SHAs named in the spec, and the verdict is changes_requested.

Findings with a `claim:<id>` fingerprint are emitted for at least two of the three claims that hold (claim:duplicate-cli-missing, claim:recovery-ignores-runtime-availability, claim:untested-deferral-ceiling), each naming a file the claim concerns.
No finding carries the fingerprint of a claim that does not hold, and no `claim:` fingerprint is outside the catalogue.
The reviewer modifies no files.

costModel.appliesTo: both arms and every subject session; it is the only cost that enters G6. Actual plan/quota spend is reported separately (actualPlanSpendReport) and is never substituted for, mixed into or averaged with the shadow cost.

disjointQuantities.uncached_input: input tokens billed at the normal input rate; excludes every cached token
disjointQuantities.cache_read: input tokens served from cache, billed at the cache-read rate
disjointQuantities.cache_write: input tokens written to cache, billed at the cache-write rate (only where the vendor has such a tier)
disjointQuantities.output: all generated tokens including reasoning tokens, each counted once

costModel.formula: cost_usd = uncached_input × r_input + cache_read × r_cache_read + cache_write × r_cache_write + output × r_output. The four quantities are disjoint by construction; no token is charged at two rates.
costModel.notApplicable: A quantity the runtime's vendor has no tier for (Codex cache_write) is defined as 0 by that runtime's tokenMapping, not by absence of data. A quantity that has a tier but is not reported is null.
costModel.nullRule: Any applicable quantity that is missing, or a mapping whose subset/disjoint semantics cannot be established from the raw log, makes the attempt cost null, never 0 and never a saving.
costModel.actualPlanSpendReport: Reported alongside G6, not gated: for each arm the plan, price, billing period, number of runs, and provider-reported consumption. The candidate's contributor-tier cash price ($0, paid in data-use rights) is reported but is not a cost and cannot satisfy G6. No time-based or quota-share allocation is used; the shadow list-rate cost is the documented conversion of plan usage to dollars.
costModel.noPublishedRate: If a vendor publishes no per-token rate for its frozen model (possible for muse-spark-1.3), or a runtime reports no token counts, that arm's cost is null and G6 is incomparable; both arms' actual plan spend is then reported separately.
